question:
A 75-year-old man presents to the physician because of bloody urine, which has occurred several times over the past month. He has no dysuria, flank pain, nausea, or vomiting. He has no history of serious illness and takes no medications. He is a 40-pack-year smoker. The vital signs are within normal limits. Physical exam shows no abnormalities except generalized lung wheezing. The laboratory test results are as follows:
Urine
Blood 3+
RBC > 100/hpf
WBC 1–2/hpf
RBC casts Negative
Bacteria Not seen
Which of the following is the most appropriate diagnostic study at this time?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Hematuria (bloody urine) -> RBC > 100/hpf -> WBC 1-2/hpf -> 80% CHAIN: Hematuria -> Blood 3+ -> RBC casts negative -> 75% CHAIN: Hematuria -> No dysuria, flank pain, nausea, or vomiting -> 70% CHAIN: Hematuria -> No history of serious illness or medications -> 65% CHAIN: Hematuria -> 40-pack-year smoker -> 60% CHAIN: Hematuria -> Generalized lung wheezing on physical exam -> 55% CHAIN: Hematuria -> No abnormalities on physical exam except lung wheezing -> 50% CHAIN: Hematuria -> Vital signs within normal limits -> 45% CHAIN: Hematuria -> No bacteria seen in urine -> 40% CHAIN: Most appropriate diagnostic study: Computed tomography (CT) urogram -> 80%
enhanced_information: The most appropriate diagnostic study at this time for the 75-year-old man with bloody urine, RBC > 100/hpf, WBC 1-2/hpf, and no other significant symptoms is a Computed Tomography (CT) urogram. This choice is supported by the consensus-aligned reasoning chains and the evidence paths do not provide additional relevant information for this specific case.
analysis: The core medical principle in this case is to investigate the cause of hematuria in a 75-year-old man with significant smoking history and no other symptoms. Given the presence of gross hematuria (RBC > 100/hpf) and the absence of other symptoms, the most appropriate diagnostic study at this time is a Computed Tomography (CT) urogram to evaluate the upper urinary tract for possible malignancy, stones, or other structural abnormalities.
